question: With every mast powered and undamaged, why do phone networks still jam in the hour after a disaster?
options: They are sized for callers acting independently
Emergency calls are given most of the lines
Crowded signals interfere with one another
answer: They are sized for independent callers. Since A. K. Erlang's work in 1917, engineers have provided lines for the chance that unrelated calls overlap: a small share of subscribers at once. A disaster makes everyone call in the same minutes. On 7 July 2005, London's mobile networks were swamped within minutes of the bombs.
move: Capacity built for separate chances fails when one event moves everyone together.
ask: Where have I planned for separate chances when one event will move everyone together?
trap: Blaming priority for emergency calls rather than everyone calling at once.
reference: London Assembly, Report of the 7 July Review Committee, Greater London Authority, 2006
